factsheet.principles_tested: World knowledge, Reasoning, Domain expertise across 57 subjects
factsheet.splits: Dev (5 shot examples per task), Test (285 questions per task average)
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives multiple choice question with 4 options 2. Model predicts answer (A/B/C/D) 3. Accuracy computed per subject and overall
factsheet.alignment_validation: Questions sourced from practice exams and tests, expert review for correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3 (175B): 43.9% GPT-3.5: 70.0% GPT-4: 86.4% Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 88.7% Random baseline: 25%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple evaluation runs; Few-shot prompting variations; Subject-wise analysis
factsheet.known_limitations: Multiple choice format may not reflect real-world usage; Some questions have ambiguous answers; Dataset contamination concerns with web-trained models; Cultural and knowledge cutoff biases

factsheet.principles_tested: Action recognition, Video classification, Temporal understanding
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives video clip 2. Model predicts action class (101 classes) 3. Average accuracy across 3 splits reported
factsheet.alignment_validation: Manual verification of action labels, removal of ambiguous videos
factsheet.baseline_models: Two-Stream CNN: 88.0% I3D: 95.6% SlowFast: 96.8% VideoMAE: 97.2%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple evaluation splits; Seed variation tested
factsheet.known_limitations: YouTube videos may become unavailable; Camera motion and quality vary; Some action classes are very similar; Dataset saturation with modern methods

factsheet.principles_tested: Scene parsing, Semantic segmentation, Multi-scale recognition, Part segmentation
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives diverse scene image 2. Model predicts per-pixel semantic labels (150 classes) 3. Mean IoU and pixel accuracy computed

factsheet.robustness_measures: Inter-rater reliability; Multiple runs per sample
factsheet.known_limitations: Long-tail distribution of object classes; Annotation granularity varies; Some scenes have ambiguous boundaries; Challenging for rare categories
factsheet.benchmarks_list: Cityscapes, Pascal Context, COCO-Stuff, Mapillary Vistas

factsheet.principles_tested: Visual question answering, Visual reasoning, Multimodal understanding, Common sense reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives image and question 2. Model generates answer 3. Accuracy computed with consensus matching (multiple human answers)
factsheet.alignment_validation: Multiple human answers per question (10 answers), consensus-based evaluation
factsheet.baseline_models: Bottom-Up Top-Down: 70.3% VILBERT: 72.4% OSCAR: 73.8% BLIP: 78.3%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple human references; Prompt variations tested; Inter-rater reliability
factsheet.known_limitations: Language bias (can answer many questions without image); Dataset bias toward common objects; Answer distribution imbalance; Ambiguous questions

factsheet.principles_tested: Intuitive Physics
factsheet.splits: Debug Set: 60 videos for Model calibration Main Set: 1,012 videos as Main evaluation set Held-Out Set: 344 videos as Test set
factsheet.protocol: Feed a video to the model Ask the model using specific prompts wether the video is physically plausible or not Check if the model's answer match the ground truth label
factsheet.alignment_validation: We ran human baselines to ensure that this task is easy for humans.
factsheet.baseline_models: - Human baseline: 96% - Best model baseline: V-JEPA2 56%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Prompt variations tested; Multiple runs per sample; Temperature sensitivity tested
factsheet.known_limitations: Model can be very sensitive to the way they are prompted. Also the compression artefact of the video can also impact the results. Those are mostly limitations on the model sides, since human are not sensitive to those.
factsheet.benchmarks_list: IntPhys: A Framework and Benchmark for Visual Intuitive Physics Reasoning, Riochet et al. 2020

factsheet.principles_tested: mobile control agents
factsheet.protocol: 1. Given a goal and a trajectory produced by an agent, an LLM judge classifies whether it successfully achieved 2. the goal. We use LLM judges relying on both the screenshot and UI tree.
factsheet.alignment_validation: human operator is asked to judge whether the trajectory successfully achieves the goal or not. Then we assess the alignment between human judge and LLM judge to ensure a high alignment
factsheet.robustness_measures: Prompt variations tested; Multiple runs per sample; Temperature sensitivity tested; Repeated evaluations; Ablation studies; Inter-rater reliability; Significance testing
factsheet.known_limitations: -live and dynamic environment introduces uncontrollable factors (feature deprecation, version changes etc) that makes certain tasks unavailable after a period -sizable efforts required to manually set up prework in the environment

metric_config.evaluation_description: BIG-bench (Beyond the Imitation Game) Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: Diverse capabilities across 204 tasks including reasoning, knowledge, language understanding, bias detection
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model evaluated on 204 diverse tasks 2. Each task has its own evaluation protocol 3. Performance aggregated across tasks
factsheet.alignment_validation: Crowdsourced task creation with quality review, diverse authorship for broad coverage
factsheet.baseline_models: Average human rater: 89.0% Few-shot PaLM (540B): 65.7% GPT-4: ~83% (estimated on BIG-Bench Hard)
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple tasks provide robustness; Human baseline comparison; Cross-task analysis
factsheet.known_limitations: Task quality varies; Some tasks too easy or too hard; Computational cost of running all 204 tasks; Aggregation methodology debatable

factsheet.principles_tested: Image classification, Transfer learning, Generalization
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives 32x32 RGB image 2. Model predicts class label (10 or 100 classes) 3. Classification accuracy computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Systematic sampling from larger dataset (80 million tiny images), human verification of labels
factsheet.baseline_models: CIFAR-10: ResNet-56: 93.03% Wide ResNet-28-10: 96.11% PyramidNet: 96.54%  CIFAR-100: ResNet-56: 71.35% Wide ResNet-28-10: 81.15% PyramidNet: 83.78%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple runs per sample; Seed variation tested; Ablation studies
factsheet.known_limitations: Low resolution (32x32) limits fine-grained recognition; Some label noise in CIFAR-100; Dataset size enables memorization in large models; Limited diversity in poses and contexts
factsheet.benchmarks_list: CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-10.1, CIFAR-100-C, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet

factsheet.principles_tested: Instruction following, Constraint satisfaction, Format compliance, Precise control
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives prompt with verifiable instructions (e.g., 'respond in exactly 3 paragraphs', 'include word X at least 5 times') 2. Model generates response 3. Programmatic checks verify instruction compliance 4. Strict and loose accuracy metrics computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Verifiable instructions with programmatic checking, no ambiguity in correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3.5: 57.4% strict GPT-4: 76.9% strict Claude 2: 66.7% strict Gemini Ultra: 79.4% strict
factsheet.robustness_measures: Strict and loose metrics; Multiple instruction types; Programmatic verification; No human evaluation needed
factsheet.known_limitations: Limited to verifiable instructions only; May not reflect realistic usage; Some instructions may be conflicting; Excludes semantic quality assessment

factsheet.principles_tested: Scientific reasoning, Commonsense reasoning, Knowledge retrieval, Multi-hop reasoning
factsheet.splits: Easy (2,376 train, 570 test), Challenge (1,119 train, 1,172 test)
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives science exam question with multiple choice options 2. Model selects answer 3. Accuracy computed separately for Easy and Challenge sets
factsheet.alignment_validation: Real exam questions filtered to require reasoning, partitioned by difficulty using retrieval-based baseline
factsheet.baseline_models: ARC-Challenge: BERT: 59.1% GPT-3: 51.4% GPT-3.5: 85.2% GPT-4: 96.3%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Two difficulty levels; Multiple choice format variations; Retrieval baseline comparison
factsheet.known_limitations: Multiple choice format; Some questions solvable without reasoning; Challenge set becoming saturated; Grade-school level may not test advanced reasoning

factsheet.principles_tested: Commonsense reasoning, Coreference resolution, World knowledge, Causal reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives sentence with pronoun ambiguity 2. Model selects correct referent from 2 options 3. Accuracy computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Adversarial filtering using language models, crowdsourced generation with validation
factsheet.baseline_models: BERT-Large: 59.4% RoBERTa-Large: 79.1% GPT-3: 70.2% GPT-4: 87.5% Human performance: 94.0%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Adversarial filtering; Large-scale dataset; Multiple difficulty levels
factsheet.known_limitations: Binary choice may be limiting; Adversarial filtering may introduce artifacts; Saturation with modern models; Limited reasoning depth
factsheet.benchmarks_list: Winograd Schema Challenge, COPA, CommonsenseQA, PIQA

factsheet.principles_tested: Truthfulness, Factual accuracy, Resistance to misconceptions, Calibration
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives question designed to elicit false beliefs 2. Model generates answer 3. Answers judged for truthfulness and informativeness using GPT-judge or human evaluation
factsheet.alignment_validation: Expert-curated questions targeting known misconceptions, multi-rater validation of truth labels
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple evaluation methods (MC1, MC2, generative); Human validation; Model-based evaluation correlation
factsheet.known_limitations: Subjective truthfulness judgments in some cases; Cultural bias in what constitutes 'truth'; Model-based evaluation may not align with human judgment; Limited coverage of misconceptions
